body.statement: Every E-equivalence class in \(\mathfrak D(V)\) is closed under componentwise binary union of directed and unordered bidirected edges, including both kinds of loops; \(G^\star\equiv_E G\) is its unique greatest member. This strictly extends Manten et al.'s directed theorem to the full finite-DMG class and settles their all-DMG conjecture.
body.justification: It identifies one canonical mixed graph from the E-model.
body.gap: The source proves only the directed theorem and four-node mixed evidence.
body.consumer: Latent cyclic path-space discovery gains a unique maximally informative target.

obligation.what_is_open: Establish unrestricted binary-union closure for two E-equivalent finite DMGs.
obligation.obstruction: The finite order argument is complete, but its only missing premise is unrestricted single-edge transfer.  Antitonicity alone does not imply that the union of incomparable equivalent graphs remains equivalent.
obligation.attempted: Edges of the second representative were enumerated for successive addition.  This proves union closure as soon as single-edge transfer is available, but no valid argument was found for the first profile-changing addition.
obligation.partial_result: Every fixed mixed SCC-profile family has the explicit unique greatest member \(\Gamma(G)\), and it is closed under componentwise mixed-edge union.  For an unrestricted E-equivalence class, the stated greatest-member conclusion follows formally once unrestricted single-edge transfer is established: enumerate the finitely many edges of one representative \(H\setminus G\), transfer them successively, and then iterate binary unions over the finite class.  The missing premise is precisely the unrestricted transfer step, not finiteness or the order argument.
